sources.entry: stagehand - A fast and token-efficient browser automation SDK to extract data and perform self-healing actions on web pages.

summary.one_liner: Stagehand is an SDK for AI browser agents that drives a real browser in TypeScript, Python, or Go, offering natural-language act, observe, and extract methods alongside Playwright-style controls.
summary.what_it_does: The SDK launches a local Chrome or a Browserbase cloud browser and exposes Playwright-style page and locator APIs. Natural-language methods let you act on a page (act), find real selectors for elements (observe), and pull schema-validated data out of a page (extract). The README says act, observe, and extract refresh how an action happens when the site changes, which it calls self-healing. Cookies can persist in a local user data directory so later runs start signed in. The README also describes search and fetch helpers that return web results or page content as markdown without opening a browser, plus a hosted Browserbase MCP server for coding agents.
use_cases: automate logins and form filling on websites
extract structured data from web pages with a schema
run AI-driven browser tasks from TypeScript, Python, or Go
give a coding agent browser access via MCP
port existing Playwright test suites to AI-assisted automation
fetch page content as markdown or run web searches without a browser
how_to_run: git clone the stagehand repo, then run: cd stagehand && just install && just generate && just build
export OPENAI_API_KEY=... and run: just example act
notable: Natural-language act, observe, and extract methods with self-healing when page layouts change
observe returns real selectors so credentials need not be sent to the model
Same API surface across TypeScript, Python, and Go
Hybrid accessibility-tree trimming to reduce tokens sent to the model
Hosted Browserbase MCP server usable from MCP clients such as Claude Code and Cursor
caveats: Local runs require Chrome to be installed
Cloud features (cache, Model Gateway, verified mode, proxies, recordings) are tied to Browserbase and an API key; the README does not detail pricing
Contributions larger than bug fixes are asked to go through maintainers first
